description:
Calming Music for Anxiety | Slow Bansuri | Indian Classical

The day ended. The tension didn't.

Something about Monday evenings — the body is still in work mode even when the work is done. The mind keeps looping on conversations, tasks that didn't finish, things you said or should have said. You're home, you're still, but you're not actually here yet.

This is 90 minutes of slow Bansuri in Raga Yaman — the classical Indian evening raga. Yaman is expansive and open. Its raised fourth interval gives it an upward, outward quality — phrases that open instead of close, that ease instead of settle. It doesn't try to sedate. It just makes space.

The bamboo flute carries it with the warmth of breath. No percussion, no rhythm to track. Just sound that gradually changes the texture of the evening.

🎵 What you'll hear:
- Bansuri — warm bamboo flute, breath-driven and slow
- Raga Yaman — the classical Indian evening raga, expansive and open
- Long sustained phrases with natural silences between them
- No percussion, no tabla — space to breathe
- A gentle theta layer barely audible underneath
- 90 unbroken minutes at 432Hz

⏱ Chapters
0:00    Still running
20:00   Beginning to slow
45:00   Tension releasing
70:00   Quiet
85:00   Still

🧠 How to use:
Press play. Don't try to relax — just let it be on. The Bansuri does the work. You just need to be in the room with it. By the time you notice it's working, it already has been for a while.

⏱ Best for:
• Anxiety that hasn't switched off after work
• Monday evening wind-down
• Mind still looping after the day ends
• Background while you cook, eat, or just sit
• Quiet company when the mind is too loud

LUFS -14 (evening viewer, awake and present). Theta 5Hz for anxiety relief. No tabla — space is essential. Bansuri mid-to-low register.
